items.title: Section: Both-Worlds-Happiness Beneficial Conduct — Guiding Beings Towards the Ten Wholesome Deeds — and Purity Beneficial Conduct Opens

items.zh: 云何菩薩此世他世樂利行？當知此行略有九種。謂諸菩薩於他有情，依淨身業。勸令遠離一切殺生；勸令遠離諸不與取；勸令遠離諸欲邪行；勸令遠離一切窣羅、若迷隸耶，及以末陀放逸處酒。依淨語業，勸令遠離一切妄語，勸令遠離諸離間語，勸令遠離諸麁惡語，勸令遠離一切綺語。依淨意業，勸令遠離一切貪欲、瞋恚、邪見。云何菩薩清淨利行？當知此行略有十種。謂諸菩薩於諸有情，依外清淨有五利行，依內清淨有五利行。云何菩薩於諸有情依外清淨有五利行？
items.en: What is a bodhisattva's beneficial conduct of happiness in this world and the next? One should know this conduct is, in brief, of nine kinds. Bodhisattvas, towards other beings, relying on pure bodily conduct, encourage them to abandon all killing; encourage them to abandon taking what is not given; encourage them to abandon sexual misconduct; and encourage them to abandon grain liquor, fermented liquor, and grape wine — intoxicants that lead to carelessness. Relying on pure verbal conduct, they encourage beings to abandon all falsehood, all divisive speech, all harsh speech, and all idle talk. Relying on pure mental conduct, they encourage beings to abandon all craving, aversion, and wrong view. What is a bodhisattva's purity beneficial conduct? One should know this conduct is, in brief, of ten kinds. Bodhisattvas, towards beings, have five kinds of beneficial conduct grounded in external purity, and five kinds grounded in internal purity.

items.title: Section: Purity Beneficial Conduct's Five External Marks — Freedom From Fault, Correcting False Paths, Gradual Teaching, Universal Reach, and Fitting Guidance

items.zh: 一、無罪利行，二、不轉利行，三、漸次利行，四、遍行利行，五、如應利行。謂諸菩薩，於諸有情雜惡行者、先惡行者、有罪行者、雜染行者，於諸善中能正安處，是名菩薩於諸有情無罪利行。又諸菩薩於諸有情，不於非解脫、非定清淨處，求為真解脫、求為定清淨者，即於其中能正勸導，是名菩薩於諸有情不轉利行。又諸菩薩，於諸有情先審觀察。知劣慧者為說淺法，隨轉麁近教授教誡；知中慧者為說中法，隨轉處中教授教誡；知廣慧者為說深法，隨轉幽微教授教誡。令其漸次修集善品，是名菩薩於諸有情漸次利行。又諸菩薩，於諸四姓乃至天人一切有情，隨力隨能行義利行、求利樂者，即於其中隨類勸導，是名菩薩於諸有情遍行利行。又諸菩薩於諸有情，若於自義諸善法品，隨下中上功能差別可勸導者，及由方便功能差別可勸導者，隨其所應，於彼、如彼方便勸導，是名菩薩於諸有情如應利行。是名菩薩於諸有情依外清淨五種利行。云何菩薩於諸有情依內清淨五種利行？
items.en: First, beneficial conduct free of fault; second, beneficial conduct correcting false paths; third, gradual beneficial conduct; fourth, universal beneficial conduct; fifth, fitting beneficial conduct. Bodhisattvas who correctly settle beings already caught in mixed unwholesome conduct, prior wrongdoing, genuinely faulty conduct, or afflicted conduct into wholesome practice — this is called a bodhisattva's beneficial conduct free of fault, towards beings. Bodhisattvas who correctly guide beings away from seeking what is not genuine liberation or genuine meditative purity as though it were — this is called a bodhisattva's beneficial conduct correcting false paths, towards beings. Bodhisattvas who first carefully observe beings, and, knowing someone of lesser wisdom, teach a correspondingly simple teaching with plain, accessible instruction; knowing someone of middling wisdom, teach a correspondingly moderate teaching; and knowing someone of broad wisdom, teach a correspondingly profound teaching with subtle, careful instruction, guiding each to gradually accumulate wholesome practice at their own pace — this is called a bodhisattva's gradual beneficial conduct, towards beings. Bodhisattvas who, towards every caste and every kind of being including the heavenly and the human, according to their own strength and ability, guide each type of being genuinely seeking benefit and ease — this is called a bodhisattva's universal beneficial conduct, towards beings. Bodhisattvas who, towards beings capable of being guided according to their own lesser, middling, or superior capacity within their own genuine spiritual concern, guide each according to the specific method genuinely fitting their own path — this is called a bodhisattva's fitting beneficial conduct, towards beings. These are a bodhisattva's five kinds of beneficial conduct grounded in external purity, towards beings.

items.title: Section: Purity Beneficial Conduct's Five Internal Marks — Humble as a Servant, Compassionate Without Retreat — Beneficial Conduct Closes Entirely

items.zh: 謂諸菩薩，於諸有情起廣大悲意樂現前而行利行。又諸菩薩，於諸有情所作義利，雖受一切大苦劬勞，而心無倦，深生歡喜，為諸有情而行利行。又諸菩薩，雖現安處最勝第一圓滿財位，而自謙下，如奴如僕，亦如孝子、旃荼羅子，其心卑屈，離憍離慢及離我執，於諸有情而行利行。又諸菩薩，於諸有情心無愛染、無有虛偽，真實哀憐而行利行。又諸菩薩，於諸有情生起畢竟無復退轉慈愍之心而行利行。是名菩薩於諸有情依內清淨五種利行。如是依於內外清淨各五利行，總有十種。是名菩薩清淨利行。
items.en: Bodhisattvas who, moved by vast compassion genuinely present before them towards beings, act with beneficial conduct accordingly. Bodhisattvas who, though undertaking every kind of great hardship and toil for the sake of beings' genuine welfare, remain entirely without fatigue, feeling instead deep genuine joy, and act with beneficial conduct towards beings on this basis. Bodhisattvas who, though presently established in the most excellent, fully complete wealth and standing, remain genuinely humble — like a servant, like a devoted son, even like the child of an outcaste — their heart genuinely lowly and yielding, free of arrogance, free of pride, and free of self-attachment, and act with beneficial conduct towards beings on this basis. Bodhisattvas whose hearts, towards beings, are free of self-interested attachment and free of any pretence, genuinely and simply compassionate, and act with beneficial conduct towards beings on this basis. Bodhisattvas who give rise to a compassion so settled towards beings that it never again retreats, and act with beneficial conduct towards beings on this basis. These are a bodhisattva's five kinds of beneficial conduct grounded in internal purity, towards beings. Together, the five kinds grounded in external purity and the five kinds grounded in internal purity make ten in all — this is called a bodhisattva's purity beneficial conduct.

items.title: Section: Working Alongside Others Opens — Leading by Example So Thoroughly No One Can Object

items.zh: 云何菩薩同事？謂諸菩薩，若於是義、於是善根勸他受學，即於此義、於此善根或等或增自現受學。如是菩薩與他事同，故名同事。所化有情知此菩薩所修同事，便於自己受學善根堅固決定，無有退轉。何以故？彼作是思：菩薩勸我所受學者，定能為我利益安樂。由此菩薩所授我者，即於其中自現行故，無有知無利益安樂自現行者。非諸菩薩如是同事勸導有情，他得詰言：汝自於善不能受學，云何以善殷勤勸導，數數教授教誡於他？汝應從他殷勤諮受、教授教誡。
items.en: What is a bodhisattva's working alongside others? Bodhisattvas who encourage others to receive and study a particular teaching or wholesome practice themselves take up and study that very same teaching or practice, matching or even exceeding what is asked — this shared undertaking of the very same activity is what is called working alongside others. Beings being guided, recognising that the bodhisattva genuinely works alongside them in this way, become correspondingly firm and decisive in their own study of that wholesome practice, never turning back. Why is this so? They reflect: "What the bodhisattva encourages me to undertake must genuinely bring me benefit and ease, since the bodhisattva personally undertakes this very thing — no one would personally undertake something they knew to be without genuine benefit." Were bodhisattvas not to guide beings by working alongside them in this way, they might rightly be challenged: "You yourself cannot even undertake what is wholesome — how can you so earnestly urge it on others, repeatedly instructing and correcting them? You yourself ought instead to be earnestly seeking instruction and correction from someone else."

blocks.text: The purity of beneficial conduct, and the fourth means: working alongside others.
Guiding beings "through pure bodily conduct" and so on towards the ten wholesome courses of action. Master Cháng Bǎi: four bodily, four verbal, one mental, nine in the treatise's count.
Free of fault; correcting false paths (Master Cháng Bǎi: some take the heaven without perception for nirvāṇa); gradual; universal; fitting.

Moved by compassion; tireless; "though in the highest position, humbling themselves as a servant, like a dutiful son, free of pride"; free of attachment; undistorted. Master Cháng Bǎi: kindness with beings as object, with phenomena as object, and without object.

"Bodhisattvas who encourage others to study a teaching or practice themselves take up that same practice, matching or exceeding them." Master Cháng Bǎi: if one leads by example, no one can object. Venerable Miào Jìng: if you don't practise yourself, others will say you have no right to teach.
The four means of embracing are a complete social ethic: give, speak kindly, help practically, and live what you teach. The last is the hardest, and the one that makes the other three believable.

quiz.q: Two-world beneficial conduct has nine kinds; the NOTE treats it as the "ten wholesome deeds." How do the lectures count nine?
options: four bodily (killing, stealing, sexual misconduct, alcohol), four verbal, and the three mental combined as one — nine
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: four bodily, four verbal, one mental — nine. Venerable Miào Jìng: the three mental count as one, plus the eight, makes nine. The NOTE's "ten wholesome deeds" omits alcohol.

quiz.q: What are the five beneficial conducts based on outer purity?
quiz.why: "First, beneficial conduct free of fault; second, correcting false paths; third, gradual; fourth, universal; fifth, fitting." Master Cháng Bǎi: arising from beings as outer conditions is outer purity; arising from one's own inner compassion is inner purity.

quiz.q: Non-diverting conduct: beings "seeking true liberation and pure concentration where there is none." What example does Master Cháng Bǎi give?
options: brahmins taking the heaven without perception as supreme nirvāṇa, and the formless absorptions as pure concentration
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: some brahmins take the heaven without perception as the highest nirvāṇa, mistaking it for liberation; others take the formless absorptions as pure concentration. Venerable Miào Jìng: only by seeing ultimate truth is there liberation.

quiz.q: Among the inner-purity conducts, though in the highest position of wealth, what is the bodhisattva's attitude?
options: humble as a servant, like a dutiful son or a caṇḍāla's son, free of pride and self-grasping
quiz.why: Though in the highest position, "humble themselves as a servant, like a dutiful son or a caṇḍāla's son, free of pride and self-grasping." Venerable Miào Jìng: "jiāo" means putting on airs — this bodhisattva doesn't.

quiz.q: "Arousing compassion that never regresses" — which three kinds of loving-kindness does Master Cháng Bǎi say ultimate kindness includes?
options: kindness with beings, with dharmas, and with no object as its basis
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the bodhisattva has all three — kindness with beings as object, with dharmas as object, and without object — called ultimate kindness. Venerable Miào Jìng: however hard beings are to save, the bodhisattva's compassion does not regress.

quiz.q: How does the treatise define "working alongside others"?
options: encouraging others in a teaching or practice while oneself practising it equally or more
quiz.why: "Bodhisattvas who encourage others to study a particular teaching or practice themselves take up that very same practice, matching or exceeding what is asked." Master Cháng Bǎi: leading by example, the bodhisattva cannot be challenged by others.

quiz.q: Without working alongside, others could object: "You yourself don't practice — how can you urge others?" What do the two lectures say?
options: Cháng Bǎi: leading by example, one cannot be challenged; Miào Jìng: if you don't practice yourself, you shouldn't pose as a spiritual friend
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: if the bodhisattva leads by example, no one can challenge them. Venerable Miào Jìng: if you don't practice yourself, you should not pose as a spiritual friend.
